name: Endermologie / LPG
lead: Endermologie, produced by the French company LPG, is a machine-assisted massage system that rolls the skin between motorised rollers while applying suction, intended to improve the look of cellulite and body contour.[1] It was originally developed in the late 1970s in France to soften scars and standardise physical therapy, and clinicians then noticed changes in contour and skin texture in treated patients.[1]

Small clinical studies have evaluated it. One study of 33 women with cellulite gave 15 sessions twice weekly, and another of 118 women used a similar schedule; both assessed cellulite grade and body measurements.[2][3] These papers describe the device as FDA-approved as a massage system, and the 2009 authors described it as lacking clinical study at that point.[2][3]
It has also been explored for lymphedema in combination with compression bandaging, a medical rather than cosmetic use.[4][5]

paras: The system applies positive-pressure rolling together with negative pressure to skin and subcutaneous tissue.[1] A 1998 report states it was developed in France in the late 1970s for scars and physical therapy, and that its body-contour use followed from observed effects of treatment.[1] Wikipedia's cellulite article lists mechanical suction and massage among non-invasive options and notes that cellulite can be resistant to many treatments.[7]

A 1998 outcome study reported one-year results of treatment for body contouring.[1] A 2009 study treated 33 healthy women with grade 1 to 3 cellulite twice weekly for 15 sessions, assessing photographs and circumference measurements.[2] A 2013 study enrolled 118 women on the same schedule and evaluated cellulite grade, safety and slimming.[3] The abstracts available do not allow a detailed account of effect sizes.

In lymphedema, a 2007 report presented two protocols combining the system with compression bandaging in women with secondary arm lymphedema, a phase II randomised trial protocol was published in 2019 for breast cancer related lymphedema, and a registered trial of a treatment pathway for breast cancer related lymphoedema exists.[4][5][6]

card.summary: A French roll-and-suction massage machine for cellulite and contour; small studies exist, large controlled evidence is thin.
card.note: Evidence is from small, short studies.

quick.overview:
Endermologie is a motorised roller-and-suction massage treatment developed in France and sold for cellulite and body contouring. It is typically studied as a course of about fifteen sessions over several weeks.

Small studies of tens to a hundred or so women report on cellulite grade and measurements, and it is also used for lymphedema alongside compression.
quick.mechanism: The device pulls and rolls the skin and the tissue beneath it with suction and rollers, a mechanical massage of subcutaneous tissue.
quick.risks: The sources reviewed describe it as FDA-approved as a massage system and do not detail adverse events in the abstracts available. Larger controlled studies were not found among them.
